name: Banke Bihari Temple, Vrindavan

mythology: Banke Bihari Temple, Vrindavan at Vrindavan, Mathura, Uttar Pradesh is dedicated to Lord Krishna (Banke Bihari), known especially for Beloved Krishna temple of Vrindavan lanes. Pilgrimage tradition places the shrine within India’s tirtha network — a seat where vows, gratitude, and family kuladevi / ishta devotion gather. Local sthala-purana and priestly teaching elaborate how Lord Krishna (Banke Bihari) blesses those who arrive with sincere intent; festival days intensify these beliefs through special alankara and community worship where practised.

Local sthala-purana and priestly teaching at Banke Bihari Temple, Vrindavan elaborate how Lord Krishna (Banke Bihari) blesses devotees who arrive with vows, gratitude, or grief. Festival days intensify these beliefs through processions, special alankara, and community feeding where practised.
